units.representation_dependency: The constructions use cycles and path integration on metric graphs; their semantic force is quotienting local divisor data by principal transformations and encoding global obstruction in a period space.
units.selection_reason: It links local chip-like divisor data to global equivalence classes, exhibits a canonical parameter space through periods, and provides a lower bound that constrains when effective representatives must exist.
units.title: Divisors, Jacobians, and Riemann-Roch on metric graphs

units.context_note: The source sketches Chern and canonical cycles, an adjunction formula, a lower bound called virtual dimension, and the regular/superabundant distinction. These are compact survey statements with no self-contained derivations in the span.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source relates discrete combinatorial types, continuous edge lengths, expected deformation dimension, compactification, and stable-map evaluation in one tropical setting. This supports the assignment-routed lens without claiming that any item is new relative to the frozen parent corpus.

units.representation_dependency: The criteria depend on tropical intersection data and affine placement of loops; they compare a global expected dimension with the locally observed deformation space.
units.selection_reason: It provides a generic diagnostic move: compute an expected parameter count from invariants, compare it with actual local freedom, and treat excess dimension as evidence of a geometric dependency or obstruction rather than ordinary behavior.
units.title: Expected deformation dimension and superabundance

units.context_note: The span parameterizes marked curves by combinatorial type and edge lengths, embeds the genus-zero space using pairwise path lengths, compactifies by infinite lengths, and introduces stable maps, evaluation, forgetting, and intersection on their moduli. Higher-genus and stable-map compactifications are presented with qualifications.

ecosystem_findings.summary: The source relates discrete combinatorial types, continuous edge lengths, expected deformation dimension, compactification, and stable-map evaluation in one tropical setting. This supports the assignment-routed lens without claiming that any item is new relative to the frozen parent corpus.

units.representation_dependency: Metric graphs and their combinatorial types provide local coordinates; compactification changes the represented object by splitting it into finite-distance components while retaining a controlled boundary interpretation.
units.selection_reason: It turns variation of objects into a parameter space, separates discrete combinatorial type from continuous edge lengths, and shows how boundary points encode degenerations rather than being discarded.
units.title: Moduli and compactification of marked tropical curves

units.context_note: The source defines classical realizability, local phases and compatibility, states realizability for regular phased tropical curves, and records superabundance as a genuine obstruction. The theorem is cited rather than proved in this survey.

ecosystem_findings.summary: Within this source, the proposed lens receives several distinct mechanisms: algebraic dequantization, passage from functions to balanced loci, auxiliary-coordinate contractions, equivalence of presentations, and enrichment by phases before lifting. This is source-level reinforcement only; comparison with the frozen parent and novelty remain unconfirmed.

units.representation_dependency: The bridge depends on logarithmic amoebas, local pair-of-pants models, and phase data that supplement the underlying tropical curve; the tropical skeleton alone is explicitly insufficient.
units.selection_reason: It exposes a useful bridge-construction principle: enrich a coarse piecewise-linear limit with compatible local phase data, then ask whether the enriched object lifts to a classical family; regularity marks the stated success boundary.
units.title: Phases, amoebas, and realizability of tropical curves

units.context_note: This is an applications section. It states, rather than proves, a correspondence between classical and tropical plane-curve counts and illustrates why local intersection multiplicities are essential when the number of visible tropical curves changes with the configuration.
units.representation_dependency: The account depends on tropical moduli, stable intersection, and a cited correspondence theorem. Its conceptual value is the weighted-count mechanism, not an independent derivation of the enumerative result.
units.selection_reason: It shows how a simpler piecewise-linear problem can stand in for a classical one only after solutions receive intrinsic multiplicities, so invariant totals survive changes that alter the unweighted solution set.
units.title: Weighted tropical counts in complex enumerative geometry

units.context_note: This is also application-level survey material. It defines signed real multiplicities and states a cited equality with Welschinger invariants; it does not supply a self-contained proof or a general-purpose construction beyond the enumerative setting.
units.representation_dependency: The mechanism depends on parity, lattice-triangle data, and a classical-to-tropical correspondence specific to real curve counts; it should not be generalized beyond that setting without further evidence.
units.selection_reason: It gives a second, distinct invariance mechanism: individual real solution counts vary, but local signs and zero contributions compress geometric behavior into a deformation-stable total.
units.title: Signed multiplicities for invariant real curve counts
